prompt: Design an implementation-ready TypeScript payment webhook handler. It must safely handle duplicate delivery, out-of-order events, concurrent processing, transient database failures, and retries. Include the storage model, transaction boundaries, pseudocode, observability, and a focused test plan.
acceptance_criteria: Defines a durable idempotency key and uniqueness constraint
Explains transaction boundaries and concurrency control
Handles duplicate and out-of-order events explicitly
Separates retryable failures from permanent failures
Includes pseudocode detailed enough to implement
Includes unit, integration, concurrency, and retry test cases
Runs no more than the configured number of attempts
Does not sleep after the final failed attempt
Provides valid TypeScript with an explicit Promise<T> return path
Tests success, eventual success, exhaustion, timing behavior, and cancellation

prompt: Create an implementation plan for migrating a production REST endpoint from offset pagination to cursor pagination without breaking existing clients. The service is TypeScript, PostgreSQL, and has mobile clients that may remain on old versions for six months.
acceptance_criteria: Defines cursor contents and stable ordering
Addresses inserts and deletes between page requests
Includes rollout, telemetry, rollback, and deprecation phases
